questions.prompt: What does Google's AI Studio agents page say about credentials you give an agent?

options.text: The agent uses only the parts of a credential its task needs.
options.explanation: The page says the opposite: it may use any credential it has access to.

options.text: The agent may use any credential it has, so grant only what you accept.
options.explanation: Right. That is why the page advises least-privilege, short-lived credentials.

options.text: Credentials are not needed, because agents work only with public data and open web pages.
options.explanation: The page gives advice for agents that log in to outside services.

questions.prompt: In Claude Code's permission rules, in what order are rules checked?

options.explanation: The docs give the reverse order. Deny comes first.

options.text: The most specific rule first, whatever its type.
options.explanation: The docs say specificity doesn't change the order.
Right. The first match in that order decides the outcome.

questions.prompt: In OpenAI's cookbook, what happens when a connector uses an agent-owned account?

options.text: Anyone it is shared with can reach what that account can reach.
options.explanation: Right. With an end-user account, each person would see only their own data.

options.text: Each user must sign in with their own account before the agent can act.
The agent can't be shared with anyone else, only its owner can use it.
options.explanation: The cookbook shares the agent with teammates. The account type decides what they can reach.
